compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues who both ask for confirmed figures during a contract renewal. That might reflect training, the same procedure or a preference for concrete information. The behaviour alone gives little information about where their profiles differ.

comparison.summary:
ESFP and ESTJ share Extraversion (E) and Sensing (S). They differ on Thinking and Feeling (T/F) and on Judging and Perceiving (J/P). In Myers-Briggs type dynamics, ESFP leads with extraverted Sensing (Se), while ESTJ leads with extraverted Thinking (Te).

- **Shared E.** Both profiles describe a preference for directing attention and energy outward. That does not establish how much someone speaks or how well they negotiate.
- **Shared S.** Sensing emphasises concrete details and experience when taking in information. People can draw on specific observations from the same meeting or consult what was recorded last time.
- **T/F.** ESFP’s F emphasises values and effects on people. ESTJ’s T emphasises logical consistency and criteria that apply across cases. Either person can consider both in a decision.
- **J/P.** ESFP’s P favours keeping options open to new information. ESTJ’s J favours structure and closure in the outside world. Both can make plans and keep commitments.

Under the convention used here, ESFP is Se–Fi–Te–Ni and ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi. They share Fi in different positions and share Te when it is used for ESFP’s tertiary Thinking. The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists alternative orientations for tertiary functions.

Either person can check figures, ask a question or make a suggestion first. What they do depends on their role, authority, deadline and information. The order cannot identify a type.

compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
In the fictional renewal, both colleagues have the same contract, pricing authority, deadline and performance records. Each row illustrates one preference or shared Sensing. Either person can use either approach.

| Shared situation | ESFP: possible emphasis | ESTJ: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both hear the same budget reduction | Confirm the stated amount and which budget it covers | Confirm the same amount and budget | Shared S: both can check concrete details |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues who both ask for confirmed figures during a contract renewal. That might reflect training, the same procedure or a preference for concrete information. The behaviour alone gives little information about where their profiles differ.

E concerns the direction of attention and energy. S concerns taking in concrete information and experience. People with the shared E and S can still pay attention to different details or arrive at different decisions.

T/F asks which considerations carry weight in a judgment. J/P asks how much someone prefers to settle or keep open in the outside world. Someone could apply strict criteria while leaving two workable arrangements open.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: what to check when a client mentions a new tender

In a fictional renewal, a client says their budget is down fifteen per cent and they may invite new bids. Both colleagues hear the same statement and have the same contract, six-week deadline and authority to refer proposed changes.

One way to take in the information is to check exactly what the client said and which budget the reduction covers. Another is to consult what happened at the previous renewal. Both illustrate Sensing and can inform the same discussion.

The colleagues could then weigh the effect of each available option on the client and service team, or test each against a consistent set of approval criteria. That distinction illustrates T/F. Either colleague can consider both.

Who asks a question or opens a record first may depend on who has the information and what the team needs to know. A single meeting does not establish a preference.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: why their dominant functions differ

Both types have E, so their dominant function faces outward in the model. ESFP’s P points to a perceiving function. Its S makes that Se, supported by introverted Feeling (Fi). ESTJ’s J points to a judging function. Its T makes that Te, supported by introverted Sensing (Si).

The convention shown here gives ESFP auxiliary Fi and tertiary Te, and ESTJ inferior Fi and dominant Te. The functions occupy different roles in the model. They do not tell you who can explain a deal, use a spreadsheet or make a decision faster.

The perceiving functions differ as written: Se and Ni for ESFP, Si and Ne for ESTJ. Both have Sensing in their four-letter code, but one uses Se as dominant and the other Si as auxiliary.

The Foundation lists Thinking (Te or Ti) as ESFP’s tertiary function and Intuition (Ne or Ni) as ESTJ’s. This article uses Te and Ne in those positions. The overlap between abbreviations depends on these choices. See the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) and the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) for each set of preferences.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The fictional examples below illustrate how people can weigh the same options. Neither says which type should handle a negotiation or pick a product.

For a shared negotiation, assign the work according to experience, access to records and who can approve terms. A practice exercise or past work is more informative about skill than a preference code.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: weighing a concession in a renewal

In a fictional renewal, a client asks for fifteen per cent off with six weeks left on the contract. Both staff members can consider the same options for price, payment, service and extras. Neither can offer a change beyond their authority.

One question is which option would help the people affected, such as whether different payment terms would ease a problem the client raised. Another is how each option fits the same criteria for cost, capacity and approval. Either colleague can ask both.

Separately, the team can settle a provisional offer or leave more than one permissible option open. This illustrates J/P under the same constraints. It does not mean offering something before it has been authorised.

A useful record lists the proposed change, its intended effect, what the team needs to confirm and who can approve it. Compare what was agreed with what was actually delivered. This checks the decision, without scoring anyone’s type.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: comparing two air conditioner quotes

In a fictional household, two people compare the same quotes for air conditioners of equal capacity. One quote costs more and includes additional installation work. They have the same budget, room measurements and service terms.

One way to assess the options is to consider what installation and follow-up would mean for the household. Another is to compare the quotes item by item against agreed requirements, such as installation work, warranty and total cost. Either person can use both.

A supplier’s explanation can clarify what is included, while a written quote gives both people something to verify. The choice depends on what they need and what the quotes support. Paying more or less cannot establish a preference.

faq_blocks.answer:
Either person can check what the feedback describes and what the records show. Then ask which available option meets the agreed criteria and what it would mean for the people involved.

faq_blocks.question: ### What if client feedback and performance records point in different directions?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. The work requires preparing the evidence, understanding the client’s priorities and knowing who can authorise a change. Assign each task according to experience and responsibility.

faq_blocks.answer:
Agree who can propose terms, what needs approval and who will record any agreement. Either person can take either role if they have the necessary information and authority.

If the client raises a new condition, clarify what was requested and who will respond. A clear handover matters more than who speaks first.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Imagine two colleagues who both ask for confirmed figures during a contract renewal. That might reflect training, the same procedure or a preference for concrete information. The behaviour alone gives little information about where their profiles differ.

E concerns the direction of attention and energy. S concerns taking in concrete information and experience. People with the shared E and S can still pay attention to different details or arrive at different decisions.

T/F asks which considerations carry weight in a judgment. J/P asks how much someone prefers to settle or keep open in the outside world. Someone could apply strict criteria while leaving two workable arrangements open.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: what to check when a client mentions a new tender

In a fictional renewal, a client says their budget is down fifteen per cent and they may invite new bids. Both colleagues hear the same statement and have the same contract, six-week deadline and authority to refer proposed changes.

One way to take in the information is to check exactly what the client said and which budget the reduction covers. Another is to consult what happened at the previous renewal. Both illustrate Sensing and can inform the same discussion.

The colleagues could then weigh the effect of each available option on the client and service team, or test each against a consistent set of approval criteria. That distinction illustrates T/F. Either colleague can consider both.

Who asks a question or opens a record first may depend on who has the information and what the team needs to know. A single meeting does not establish a preference.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: why their dominant functions differ

Both types have E, so their dominant function faces outward in the model. ESFP’s P points to a perceiving function. Its S makes that Se, supported by introverted Feeling (Fi). ESTJ’s J points to a judging function. Its T makes that Te, supported by introverted Sensing (Si).

The convention shown here gives ESFP auxiliary Fi and tertiary Te, and ESTJ inferior Fi and dominant Te. The functions occupy different roles in the model. They do not tell you who can explain a deal, use a spreadsheet or make a decision faster.

The perceiving functions differ as written: Se and Ni for ESFP, Si and Ne for ESTJ. Both have Sensing in their four-letter code, but one uses Se as dominant and the other Si as auxiliary.

The Foundation lists Thinking (Te or Ti) as ESFP’s tertiary function and Intuition (Ne or Ni) as ESTJ’s. This article uses Te and Ne in those positions. The overlap between abbreviations depends on these choices. See the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) and the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) for each set of preferences.

sections.body_md:
In the fictional renewal, both colleagues have the same contract, pricing authority, deadline and performance records. Each row illustrates one preference or shared Sensing. Either person can use either approach.

| Shared situation | ESFP: possible emphasis | ESTJ: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both hear the same budget reduction | Confirm the stated amount and which budget it covers | Confirm the same amount and budget | Shared S: both can check concrete details |
| Both review the same concessions | Weigh what each concession would mean for the client and the team delivering it | Weigh each concession against the same agreed cost and approval criteria | T/F: effects on people or consistently applied criteria |
| The client adds the same late condition | Keep several feasible versions open until the next review | Set a provisional version that can be revisited at the same review | J/P: keeping options open or setting a provisional plan |
| Both prepare for the next meeting | Compare the current statement with the previous renewal record | Compare the same statement with the same record | Shared S: both can draw on concrete information and experience |
| Both need to arrange another meeting | Keep more than one time or format open within the same deadline | Agree on a provisional time and format within the same deadline | J/P: how much to settle in advance |
| Reviewing the same concessions after the meeting | Weigh the documented effects on the client and service team | Apply the same review criteria to each approved concession and its outcome | T/F: effects on people or consistency of evaluation |

Experience, timing and authority can explain what a person does. The table illustrates the preferences and cannot identify a type or predict who is more likely to reach an agreement.
sections.title: ESFP and ESTJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
The fictional examples below illustrate how people can weigh the same options. Neither says which type should handle a negotiation or pick a product.

For a shared negotiation, assign the work according to experience, access to records and who can approve terms. A practice exercise or past work is more informative about skill than a preference code.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: weighing a concession in a renewal

In a fictional renewal, a client asks for fifteen per cent off with six weeks left on the contract. Both staff members can consider the same options for price, payment, service and extras. Neither can offer a change beyond their authority.

One question is which option would help the people affected, such as whether different payment terms would ease a problem the client raised. Another is how each option fits the same criteria for cost, capacity and approval. Either colleague can ask both.

Separately, the team can settle a provisional offer or leave more than one permissible option open. This illustrates J/P under the same constraints. It does not mean offering something before it has been authorised.

A useful record lists the proposed change, its intended effect, what the team needs to confirm and who can approve it. Compare what was agreed with what was actually delivered. This checks the decision, without scoring anyone’s type.

### ### ESFP and ESTJ: comparing two air conditioner quotes

In a fictional household, two people compare the same quotes for air conditioners of equal capacity. One quote costs more and includes additional installation work. They have the same budget, room measurements and service terms.

One way to assess the options is to consider what installation and follow-up would mean for the household. Another is to compare the quotes item by item against agreed requirements, such as installation work, warranty and total cost. Either person can use both.

A supplier’s explanation can clarify what is included, while a written quote gives both people something to verify. The choice depends on what they need and what the quotes support. Paying more or less cannot establish a preference.
sections.title: ESFP and ESTJ at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
ESFP’s preference code does not indicate numeracy. Anyone trained to review costs can use a spreadsheet, and either type can make an estimate based on experience.

ESTJ’s Thinking preference does not describe their warmth or commitment to a value. Either type can take people’s concerns seriously and ask that a standard be applied consistently.

A firm tone can reflect the setting, the stakes or the speaker’s responsibilities. How forcefully someone negotiates tells you little about T/F or J/P.

Checking figures, asking a question or changing a plan first can depend on what information is available and who is authorised to act. The order cannot identify a type.

sections.body_md:
If results differ, compare the instruments, versions, languages and scoring. Use the instrument’s own guidance on T/F and J/P scores and cutoffs if it provides them. The labels alone cannot tell you how close either score was.

Think about what you used as a reference when answering. A job may require you to meet a deadline, give a firm reply or consider a customer’s circumstances. Those demands affect which examples come to mind.

Pick several occasions where you had a genuine choice. Note which considerations influenced the decision and which parts of the plan you chose to settle or keep open. Record a constraint or counterexample as well.

Use the notes to explain your own choices. They cannot determine your type or test the reliability of a questionnaire.
sections.title: ESFP and ESTJ: how to keep observing

items.answer:
They share E and S but differ on T/F and J/P. T/F concerns the reasons that carry weight in a judgment. J/P concerns how much structure or openness a person prefers in the outside world.

Either type can use the same figures and make the same plan. A preference can help describe a consideration someone weighs, but one decision or action cannot identify a type.
items.question: ### What is the main difference between ESFP and ESTJ?

items.answer:
Under the notation used here, they share Fi and Te. Fi is auxiliary for ESFP and inferior for ESTJ. Te is tertiary for ESFP and dominant for ESTJ.

The shared Fi does not depend on the tertiary notation. The shared Te does, because the Foundation also allows Ti for ESFP’s tertiary Thinking. Neither position predicts a person’s skill.
items.question: ### Which cognitive functions do ESFP and ESTJ share?

items.answer:
Either person can check what the feedback describes and what the records show. Then ask which available option meets the agreed criteria and what it would mean for the people involved.

Make the decision within the same authority and deadline. Note what you could verify and what remained uncertain. This helps explain the decision without treating it as evidence of type.
items.question: ### What if client feedback and performance records point in different directions?

items.answer:
Yes. The work requires preparing the evidence, understanding the client’s priorities and knowing who can authorise a change. Assign each task according to experience and responsibility.

To explore the work, try summarising a fictional client’s request and comparing two permitted options. Consider which parts you want to practise and how they relate to an actual account or procurement role.
items.question: ### Can either type handle a contract renewal?

items.answer:
Agree who can propose terms, what needs approval and who will record any agreement. Either person can take either role if they have the necessary information and authority.

If the client raises a new condition, clarify what was requested and who will respond. A clear handover matters more than who speaks first.
